newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters apologises for dispute with MP.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters apologises for dispute with MP.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters on Thursday offered an "unreserved apology" to National party MP John Banks over an incident in a corridor of parliament on Wednesday night.
Peters, who earlier denied allegations by Banks that the Treasurer abused and assaulted him, did not comment in any further detail.
Peters said the two men had had a dispute which had "clearly upset" Banks.
"I wish to tender my apology to him unreservedly," Peters told parliament.
Earlier, left-wing Alliance party leader Jim Anderton backed Banks' contention that Peters had manhandled him.
"He grabbed Mr Banks -- and by grabbing I mean he grabbed him quite strongly by the shoulder -- and was either shaking him or physically pushing him across the corridor," Anderton said.
Anderton also said Peters' colleague, Maori Affairs Minister Tau Henare, had physically prevented a Radio New Zealand reporter from tape-recording the incident.
Peters is Treasurer and Deputy Prime Minister in a centre-right coalition between his New Zealand First party and the conservative National Party.
Banks is a backbench National MP and former cabinet minister.
"I was assaulted. I was grabbed by the shoulder and close to the scruff of the neck and given one hell of a good shake and push," Banks said.
Peters, interviewed earlier on Radio New Zealand, said upsetting someone's feelings did not constitute an assault.

"We were walking down the corridor side by side having a strong conversation. That's not an assault, that's not an abuse, and you'd have to get a forensic scientist to try and find anything that would back that up."

Pressed on whether he made physical contact with Banks, Peters said: "We were walking down the corridor side by side. If I brushed him and he brushed me as we were talking, that's just pretty normal, isn't it?"
